The resonator_obs level shift and autocorrelation are statistical artifacts. The z=13.5 is a false positive arising from post-hoc selection bias (looking for level changes after observing the data); the 13-day autocorrelation is within chance bounds (±0.483) with small n=36. All four instruments are genuinely stable; resonator_obs readings are just noise.

Resonator_obs baseline (days 1–10) was recorded during incomplete thermal or optical transient; post-day-18 readings represent true stable equilibrium; days 11–17 were slow equilibration phase. The instrument was not ready for baseline on day 1.

Resonator_obs underwent a real physical transition around day 18: thermal creep, mechanical settling, or location-specific environmental shift (temperature, humidity, vibration) affecting cavity resonance. The positive level shift and 8-day autocorrelation reflect genuine instrumental/environmental dynamics at the observatory site, not at the lab.

Resonator_obs is located in a thermally isolated observatory with higher thermal inertia; a localized environmental event (thermal transient, HVAC cycle, or solar loading pattern) around day 17–18 affected only resonator_obs; resonator_lab (indoors, different thermal environment) was unaffected.

Resonator_obs exhibits genuine instrumental drift or environmental sensitivity; other instruments are stable. The positive drift and autocorrelation lag suggest a slow physical change — thermal creep in the resonator, mounting stress relief, or a systematic environmental factor (e.g., settling vibration) affecting only the observatory location.

A systematic offset or gain error introduced early could appear as apparent drift if baseline measurements were biased or if the instrument's response changed relative to a reference. Recalibration needed.
